item.title: Fuel prices today on 8 November: Check how much petrol, diesel cost in Delhi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Chennai — Full list
item.description: Petrol and diesel prices remained largely unchanged across major Indian cities on November 8, despite fluctuations in global crude rates amid Middle East tensions. Meanwhile, India's oil consumption surged 10% in October to its highest level since March, government data showed.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: Fuel prices today, November 8: Petrol and diesel prices remained largely unchanged on Sunday (November 8) across most major cities, including New Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai and Mumbai. However, minor fluctuations were observed in some other cities, such as Gurugram.Fuel prices have remained largely stable, with only marginal fluctuations, over the past two months. Last month, the Finance Ministry announced a revised duty structure, which came into effect on October 31. Under the revised structure, the export duty on petrol was reduced to zero from ₹2.50 per litre. However, the levy on diesel was increased from ₹8.50 per litre to ₹11.50 per litre.While tensions in the Middle East have triggered fluctuations in global oil prices, Indian fuel retailers have largely kept domestic petrol and diesel rates unchanged. This has shielded consumers from the impact of international price movements, offering some relief amid a period of geopolitical turmoil and uncertainty.Fuel prices generally vary across cities and states due to factors such as freight charges, local taxes, including Value Added Tax (VAT), and other regional considerations.Check the latest petrol and diesel prices in your city on November 8:*Source: GoodreturnsIndia's October fuel demand soars to its highest level since MarchIndia's oil consumption rose by around 10% in October to 20.49 million metric tonnes, compared with 18.71 million metric tonnes in September, marking its highest level since March this year. Citing data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the Oil Ministry, Reuters reported that October consumption was 2.7% higher than in the same month last year.Diesel consumption surged 19% in October compared with September, while recording a 12% increase year-on-year. Gasoline sales also rose 3.5% from the corresponding period last year.Meanwhile, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) consumption declined marginally by around 1% in October to 2.52 million metric tonnes compared with September. It was also down approximately 12.3% from a year earlier.Crude prices jump on Friday amid renewed fears of US attack on IranOil prices edged higher on Friday (local time) amid concerns over a possible escalation of US military action against Iran. US President Donald Trump said he would soon decide whether to pursue a peace agreement with Tehran or launch further strikes to weaken the Islamic Republic.Brent crude futures for January delivery settled at $98.32 per barrel, gaining 3 cents, or 0.03%. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures ended at $90.83 per barrel, up 31 cents, or 0.34%.However, both benchmarks remained on track for significant weekly losses. Brent crude was poised to record a decline of nearly 17% for the week. If sustained, this would mark its steepest weekly percentage fall since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and its biggest decline in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.WTI crude was also heading for a weekly decline of approximately 13%.

item.title: Gunman Kills Six People in Krakow, Polish Police Say
item.description: The gunman who killed six people in the historic Old Town district of Poland’s second largest city on Saturday is likely a domestic far-right extremist, according to Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- The gunman who killed six people in the historic Old Town district of Poland’s second largest city on Saturday is likely a domestic far-right extremist, according to Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski.The alleged perpetrator, a 24-year-old Polish national whose name hasn’t been made public, was injured during an exchange of gunfire with police near the Main Market Square in Krakow and taken to the hospital, where he’s undergoing an operation, Kierwinski said.The suspect drove onto the main Krakow square in a car and opened fire with an automatic rifle at what appeared to be random targets, according to government officials. Those killed included four women and two men, while a further 16 people were injured, the regional police said. Three police officers were injured in the shooting, including one with several wounds in critical condition in a Krakow hospital, Kierwinski said.“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideology,” Kierwinski told reporters in Krakow. Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland was dealing with an act of terrorism.Video taken by a witness and showed by broadcaster TVN24 showed the suspected shooter apparently injured, laying on a sidewalk, dressed in military gear, a bullet proof vest and with a rifle. The defense minister said the suspect had no links to the Polish military.Kierwinski said the suspect had a license for a firearm and that his car was full of ammunition and other guns that probably belong to his family. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said police are looking into “all the circumstances of the attack,” while President President Karol Nawrocki said he’s in contact with the relevant authorities and expects a full explanation of the circumstances. The district in Krakow, a city of some 800,000 located about 250 km (150 miles) south of Warsaw, is a Unesco World Heritage Site known for its medieval architecture. It’s a popular destination for tourists. (Updates with details about the suspect, from the first paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
